items.title: 【Claude Fable 5.2 の effort を high から max に上げたら、トークンも時間も約4倍、見つけたバグの数は同じでした】
items.summary:
【Claude Fable 5.2 の effort を high から max に上げたら、トークンも時間も約4倍、見つけたバグの数は同じでした】

high・xhigh・max の3つで同じ問題を解かせた、自前の実験の結果です

Claude Codeには「effort（エフォート）」という設定があります
AIにどれだけ念入りに作業させるかを選ぶ物で、上げるほどトークンも時間もかかります

max は、トークンの消費が半端ないです
普段から max にしている人は、少ないと思います

では、その分だけ結果は良くなるのか
そこを確かめました

先に結果を書きます

・見つけたバグの数は、3つとも同じでした（全部見つけてます）
・変わったのはトークンと時間で、max は high の約4倍
・細かい所の質は、上の設定の方が少し良かった
・費用と質のバランスが一番良かったのは、真ん中の xhigh

ただ、各設定2回ずつの小さな実験です
「max は無駄」とまでは言えません
その理由も書きます

▼どうやって比べたか

問題は、別の会社のAIに作らせました
OpenAIの GPT-6 Astra です

Claudeの系統のAIが出題すると、Claudeが見落としやすい所と重なって、甘い試験になるからです

仕込んだバグは、全部プログラムを実際に動かして、本物だと確かめてあります

解く側は、Claude Codeを画面なしで自動実行して、ファイルを読む道具だけを使わせました

採点は、誰の答えかを伏せた上で、GPT-6 Astra と Claude Opus 5.5 が別々にやってます
解く側が正解表を一度も読んでいない事も、実行の記録で確かめました

同じ問題を設定ごとに2回ずつ、全部で24回です

▼まず、普通の難しさで

ECサイトの決済のコードに、バグを10個仕込みました
「正しいのに怪しく見える」ひっかけも3個入れてます

結果は、3つとも10個全部を発見
ひっかけを間違って指摘した回数もゼロでした

障害の原因を当てる問題も、3つとも正解です

これでは差が分からないので、難しくして作り直しました

▼次に、かなり難しくして

約750行のコードに、バグを14個
ひっかけは5個です

14個のうち4個は、出題したAIが「熟練者が1回読んで見つけられるのは30%程度」と見込んだ物でした
夏時間に切り替わる日の時刻の比較や、同時に書き込んだ時の失敗などです

もう1問は、543行の生のログから障害の原因を突き止める問題
2台のサーバーの時計が約87秒ずれていて、答えをまとめた行は1行もありません

それでも、3つとも14個全部を発見
ログの問題も、採点した8項目が全部正解でした

3つの中で一番軽い high が、2回とも全部見抜いてます

▼違ったのは、トークンと時間

難しくした方のコードの問題、1回あたりの数字です

・high　出力 約2.3万トークン、約4.2分
・xhigh　出力 約5.1万トークン、約8.8分
・max　出力 約10.9万トークン、約18分

max は high と比べて、トークンが約4.7倍、時間が約4.3倍です
問題によって幅があって、トークンは約3.6〜4.7倍、時間は約3.5〜4.3倍でした

トークンは、AIが読み書きする量の単位です
料金や使用量の元になります

APIの定価に直すと、1回あたり high が約1.2ドル、xhigh が約2.4ドル、max が約5.0ドルでした
定額のプランなら、この金額が請求されるわけではないです

▼差が出たのは、細かい所

1つ目は、バグの深刻さの付け方です
正解表と合っていた割合は、平均で high が約58%、xhigh が約72%、max が約77%でした

2つ目は、ログを引用する時の正確さです
引用の誤りは、全体で high が9件、xhigh が5件、max が3件でした（GPT-6 Astraの判定）

ただ、xhigh と max の差は小さいです
深刻さの付け方は、普通の難しさの方では max、難しくした方では xhigh の方が合っていて、順番が入れ替わってます

▼やってみて面白かった事

max だけ、読み直しが増えてました
ログの問題で、ファイルを読むなどのやり取りは、high と xhigh が16回、max が25回です
それでも、結論の正しさは変わりませんでした

もう1つは、採点するAIにも好みが出た事です
答えの中に「9月にも同じ問題が起きていたはず」という、証拠から一歩踏み込んだ推測がありました
Claudeは役に立つ警告として加点して、GPT-6 Astraは根拠を超えた推測として減点してます

▼この実験で言えない事

・各設定2回ずつ、全部で24回の小さな実験です
・問題は人工的に作った物なので、実際のコード全部に当てはまるとは限りません
・難しくしても high が満点だったので、「max でないと解けない難しさ」は測れていません
・深刻さの正解は、出題したAI 1つの判断です
・時間は、3〜6本を同時に動かした時の値です（3つは常に同時に動かしたので、比べる条件はそろってます）
・high より下の設定は、比べていません

なので「max は無駄」とは言えません
言えるのは、「この問題では、設定を上げても見つかる数は増えなかった」までです

正直、「max は無駄でした」と言い切った方が伸びると思います
でも、そこまで言える実験ではないので言いません

▼公式の説明とも合ってました

Anthropicの公式の説明では、effort は「考える深さ」だけの設定ではないです
返答の文章にも、ファイルを読むなどの道具の呼び出しにも、考える量にも影響する、とされてます

max だけ読み直しが増えたのは、この説明と合ってます

Claude Codeの公式の説明には、max は効果が頭打ちになる事があって、考え過ぎる傾向があるので、広く使う前に試すように、とも書かれてます

今回は、それを自分の問題で確かめた形です

▼来そうな質問に先に答えておきます

「じゃあ high で十分？」
→ 見つける数は同じでしたが、深刻さの付け方や引用の正確さは、上の設定の方が少し良かったです
いつも high で良い、とは言えません

「定額のプランなら、トークンは気にしなくていい？」
→ 金額は請求されませんが、時間は約4倍かかります
公式の説明でも、effort を上げるほど使用量の上限に早く届く、とされてます

「AIが作った問題を、AIが採点して意味がある？」
→ そこは弱い所です
なので、出題と採点を別の会社のAIにして、誰の答えかを伏せました
バグが本物かどうかは、プログラムを動かして確かめてあります

▼まとめ

・Claude Fable 5.2 の effort を、high・xhigh・max で比べた（全24回）
・見つけたバグの数は、3つとも同じ
・max は high の約4倍のトークンと時間がかかった
・細かい所の質は上の設定が少し良く、バランスは xhigh が一番良かった
・小さな実験なので、「max は無駄」とは言えない

「ここは max でないと駄目だった」という場面があれば、教えてください

[...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

The workplace-video resources describe possible tasks in areas including warehousing, maintenance, construction, production and vehicle service. These examples are discussion starting points, not confirmed eligible categories. The guidance asks owners to review participant consent, recording permissions, safety, equipment and footage acceptance criteria before beginning. [...] DataLogix AI, a division of Trailblaze Solutions LLC, has launched online resources to help business owners explore first-person workplace video for AI and robotics training. The new resources include a workplace-video overview, an adjustable revenue calculator, a business owner guide and an inquiry form for discussing potential fit. [...] Businesses interested in learning more can use the inquiry form to describe their company and the opportunity they would like to discuss. An inquiry is not enrollment, recording permission or a payment offer. Program availability, equipment and commercial terms require separate confirmation, and payment may be zero.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
